description: BE AN EARTH TREND COOLEST DETECTIVE
summary:
NE-AR transforms NASA’s “Be an Earth System Trend Detective” challenge into an immersive and interactive exploration of how our planet is changing.

We developed an integrated platform comprising a web-based Augmented Reality (AR) experience, an interactive website, and an educational eBook. Using NASA Earth observation data, NE-AR enables users to investigate environmental trends using examples of three critical Indian ecosystems: the Himalayan glaciers, the Thar Desert, and the Sundarbans. It helps users uncover what is changing, where changes are occurring, by how much, and whether observed trends are statistically significant.

Through interactive 3D landscapes, adjustable environmental parameters, and future timelines, users can explore environmental changes and compare potential future scenarios with and without interventions.

By transforming complex scientific datasets into accessible, visual, and interactive experiences, NE-AR bridges the gap between Earth science research and public understanding. It empowers people to move beyond simply observing environmental change, encouraging them to investigate its patterns, understand its consequences, and recognize how informed decisions can help shape a more sustainable future.
details:
The Earth is speaking through data. NE-AR helps us listen, investigate, and understand what lies ahead

What NE-AR does

NE-AR (Naturalists Explorer- Augmented Reality) is an interactive Earth science platform that investigates a fundamental question: How is the climate changing across different regions, and how significant are those changes?

Developed around three geographically and ecologically distinct regions, the Western Himalayas, the Thar Desert, and the Sundarbans, NE-AR integrates four components: an interactive website with a built in statistical trend detection algorithm, a web-based Augmented Reality experience, an educational eBook, and a guided project demonstration.

Project links:

Website and Trend Detective: https://vivivarm.github.io/ne-ar-trend-detective/

eBook: https://ne-ar-diaries-indo-gangetic.netlify.app

AR web version (opens in the browser on Android and iPhone): https://climate-detective.vercel.app/

AR app for Android (NE-AR 1.0.1, .apk): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HQA_0hNr_d0uB5_ysqrFBMOPcqrqJ5OV/view?usp=sharing

How it works

The website functions as an interactive Trend Detective. Users select an environmental variable, such as temperature, rainfall, snow depth, humidity, or soil moisture, and choose a study region.

The platform retrieves 45 years of monthly NASA POWER data, covering 1981 to 2025. It aggregates the observations geographically and converts monthly measurements into annual values for trend analysis.

Its statistical engine performs the Mann Kendall trend test to determine the direction and statistical significance of observed changes. Sen’s slope estimates the magnitude and rate of change per decade. Recent observations are also compared against the 1981 to 2010 climatological baseline to identify unusual conditions. Importantly, users can examine the individual calculation steps rather than simply receiving a final result.

The platform then presents future climate projections through NASA NEX GDDP CMIP6 data, using four climate models: ACCESS CM2, MIROC6, MRI ESM2 0, and GFDL ESM4. Users can explore projections extending to 2100 under two contrasting emissions pathways, SSP2 at 4.5 and SSP5 at 8.5, to understand how different emissions trajectories may influence future environmental conditions.

A single tap connects the investigation to the AR web version, where users can explore the selected region through interactive Augmented Reality models.

For additional environmental context, we incorporated two independent NASA aerosol datasets, MERRA 2 and MODIS Aqua, allowing observations from a satellite instrument to be compared with those from a reanalysis dataset.

It also shows how conditions could look with and without action, using NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate projections (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5).

The e-book acts as a user educational guide for them to become the trend detective and know its relevance and uses.

Scientific findings

Our analysis produced several notable regional findings:

  1. Western Himalaya: Snow depth shows an increasing trend of 1.0 cm per decade (p < 0.001).
  2. Thar Desert: Annual average temperature shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.55). However, minimum temperature is increasing by 0.26°C per decade (p = 0.002), highlighting warming during cooler periods.
  3. Sundarbans: Rainfall shows an increasing trend of 0.68 mm per day per decade (p < 0.001).

These findings demonstrate why examining individual environmental variables matters. A single regional temperature average may conceal important changes in other components of the climate system.

Scientific validation and reliability

Statistical accuracy and reproducibility were central to our development process. We built an independent Python validation engine using Mann Kendall, Seasonal Mann Kendall, Correlated Seasonal Mann Kendall, Sen’s slope, ordinary least squares regression, and autocorrelation diagnostics using ACF and Ljung Box tests.

We validated the website’s JavaScript calculations against 52 independent test series. Results were compared with SciPy and pymannkendall implementations. The platform also passed 56 automated tests across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices. The eBook calculations were independently recomputed and matched the reported results.

This additional validation helps ensure that our platform distinguishes statistically meaningful trends from apparent patterns that may arise from natural variability or autocorrelation.

Benefits and intended impact

NE-AR makes Earth science more accessible without compromising scientific transparency. Users do not need prior knowledge of programming, statistical analysis, or climate modelling to investigate environmental trends.

Its key benefits include:

  1. Scientific accessibility: Complex NASA datasets become understandable through interactive investigations and visual explanations.
  2. Statistical transparency: Users can inspect the calculations and understand how conclusions are derived rather than relying on unexplained graphs or headlines.
  3. Regional relevance: Students and communities can explore environmental changes in regions that are geographically and ecologically important.
  4. Future awareness: Comparing alternative emissions pathways helps users understand how present and future choices may influence environmental outcomes.
  5. Open accessibility: The browser based platform uses freely available NASA data and can be accessed across devices.

Our intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, environmental awareness, and data literacy. We want students and people living in these regions to investigate climate claims about their own surroundings using scientific evidence, empowering them to become informed participants in understanding environmental change.

Creativity and innovation

The central innovation of NE-AR is the integration of statistical investigation, geographic visualization, Augmented Reality, and future climate scenarios into one connected experience.

Instead of presenting climate change as a collection of static graphs, NE-AR turns scientific exploration into a guided investigation. Its Trend Detective interface encourages users to ask questions, select variables, examine statistical evidence, and explore possible futures. The AR component adds a spatial dimension to the investigation, while the eBook provides a structured educational resource.

We designed the experience around scientific accuracy, reproducibility, ease of use, regional relevance, cross device compatibility, and the ability to communicate complex information to audiences with different levels of scientific knowledge.

Technologies and resources used

Website: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, qrcode generator, model-viewer for web AR (GLB and USDZ 3D data models that open on iPhone and Android with no app), and Chatbase for the NE-AR Guide. It includes an English/Spanish version, offline support and a live news feed from NASA EONET. Hosted on GitHub Pages.

Statistical validation: Python, SciPy, and pymannkendall.

Educational eBook: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS version 4, Gullabs React Flipbook, qrcode, lucide react, and Framer Motion. Hosted on Netlify.

NASA data and services:

  1. NASA POWER API: Monthly environmental observations from 1981 to 2025, including temperature, rainfall, humidity, snow depth, and soil moisture variables.
  2. NASA MERRA 2: M2TMNXAER aerosol extinction data at 550 nm.
  3. NASA MODIS Aqua: MYD08 M3 Collection 6.1 aerosol observations.
  4. NASA NEX GDDP CMIP6: Future climate projections from four climate models under two emissions pathways.
  5. NASA GIBS: VIIRS Black Marble 2016 night light imagery, used for the eBook cover.
  6. NASA Giovanni and KNMI Climate Explorer: Data exploration and independent cross verification using the challenge resources.

The 3D data models and project branding were developed by our team. AI-generated illustrations, including the wizard, the NE-AR logo/badge and the astronaut, are labelled on the website. AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) supported coding and testing; the team defined the concept, methods and content, and the statistics were validated independently.

Future development

We aim to expand the platform to additional geographical regions and integrate GRACE FO observations to investigate changes in Himalayan terrestrial water storage. This would extend NE-AR beyond atmospheric and surface variables to include another important dimension of the Earth system.

Every trend is a clue. Every dataset tells a story. With NE-AR, we decode a changing Earth and discover what comes next.
